newsitem.title: USA: Kazakstan Goldfields ships first gold.
newsitem.headline: Kazakstan Goldfields ships first gold.

text.p: Kazakstan Goldfields Corp, controlled by Canadian mining interests, said Wednesday it has completed its first gold shipment and sale from its mines in north central Kazakstan.
A total of 2,500 ounces were shipped to London for refining in late December, with a further 1,000 ounces due to be shipped by the end of this week, company president Charles Pitcher said.

The company also announced it had completed a US$1.5 million short term production loan facility with Gerald Metals Inc of the US, an international metals financier. The facility is secured against gold production and sales to Gerald Metals.
An additional 7,500 ounces of gold contained in 4,500 tonnes of flotation concentrates are being processed at the Balkhash smelter in eastern Kazakstan, Pitcher said.
But the Balkhash smelter has advised KGFC that it is currently only capable of processing 100 tonnes of KGFC concentrates per day.
As a result KGFC has decided to accelerate its plans to acquire and install a carbon-in-leach (CIL) facility.
The CIL facility will be capable of processing output from all three of the company's mines, eliminating reliance on the Balkhash smelter.

In a related move, KGFC has increased operations at its Bestobe mine and expects to be producing 4,500 ounces per month by March, 50 pct of which will be gravity concentrate, at an all inclusive cost of US$285 per ounce.

In March 1996, KGFC acquired the gold mines of the Kazakhstan state-owned enterprise, Kazakhaltyn, which produced 10 million ounces of gold in recent years, and has remaining resources of about three million ounces.
An unlisted public company, KGFC has been quoted on the Canadian Dealing Network under the symbol KGFC since October 1996.
